extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and USPTO examiners handling applications with nucleotide/amino acid sequence disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Ensure nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosures in U.S. patent applications comply with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 and the MPEP requirements for Sequence Listings, computer readable forms (CRFs), symbols, feature keys, submission formats, and cure procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive conformity to 37 CFR 1.821–1.825
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications which contain disclosures of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences ... shall, with regard to the manner in which the nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences are presented and described, conform exclusively to the requirements of §§ 1.821 through 1.825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence rules define mandatory symbols and procedures that are the only permitted way to describe information in the Sequence Listing. 37 CFR 1.822–1.824 set forth detailed, mandatory presentation requirements; 1.825 sets procedures for adding/replacing Sequence Listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'sequence' and applicability thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences, as used in §§ 1.821 through 1.825, are interpreted to mean an unbranched sequence of 4 or more amino acids or an unbranched sequence of 10 or more nucleotides. Sequences with fewer than four specifically defined nucleotides or amino acids are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Specifically defined' excludes Xaa (amino acids) and n (nucleotides) per the Appendices. Branched sequences and D-amino-acid-containing sequences are excluded from the definition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing must be a separate part of the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications that contain disclosures of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences ... must contain a 'Sequence Listing,' which is a separate part of the specification containing each of those sequences and associated information using the symbols and format in accordance with §§ 1.822 and 1.823.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sequence Listing must present each sequence and associated data using the required format and symbols; see MPEP § 2422.03 and § 2422.04 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission formats for the Sequence Listing
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sequence Listing' must be submitted as: (1) an ASCII plain text file (compliance with § 1.824) via the USPTO electronic filing system or on a read-only optical disc accompanied by an incorporation by reference statement; (2) as a PDF file via the USPTO electronic filing system; or (3) on physical sheets of paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitted as ASCII plain text, follow § 1.824 requirements. If submitted as PDF or paper, additional CRF requirements (see paragraph (e)) apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer Readable Form (CRF) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.821(e) requires a separate computer readable form (CRF) of the 'Sequence Listing' under certain circumstances. The CRF is an ASCII plain text file of the sequence information using the symbols, format, content and file requirements of 37 CFR 1.822 and 1.824.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CRF may be submitted on read-only optical disc or as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO electronic filing system. Detailed requirements are in § 1.824 and MPEP § 2422.04. The CRF may not be retained as part of the patent application file.

rubrics_metrics.name: When PDF or paper Sequence Listing is filed, CRF and identity statement required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing is submitted as a PDF file or on physical sheets, then a CRF of the Sequence Listing must be submitted and a statement that the sequence information in the CRF is identical to that in the Sequence Listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This applies to applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and to international national stage entries; see paragraphs (e)(1) and (e)(2) for exact requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence identifier reference requirement in descriptions, claims and drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the description or claims of a patent application discuss a sequence that is set forth in the Sequence Listing, reference must be made to the sequence by use of the sequence identifier (§ 1.823(a)(5)), preceded by 'SEQ ID NO:' or the like, in the text of the description or claims, even if the sequence is embedded in the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sequence appears in a drawing, the sequence must be referenced by the sequence identifier either in the drawing or in the Brief Description of the Drawings with a clear correlation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of sequence rules to all sequences in the application
rubrics_metrics.description: The sequence rules embrace all unbranched nucleotide sequences with ten or more nucleotide bases and all unbranched, non-D amino acid sequences with four or more amino acids ... The rules apply to all sequences in a given application, whether claimed or not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All such sequences must be included to support building a comprehensive database and properly assessing prior art; omission may affect search/examination and database completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unreadable or missing CRFs and early notifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants whose computer readable forms are not readable, or are missing mandatory elements, will be notified shortly after receipt of the application by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPAP will mail a notice listing unmet requirements and provide a two-month period to comply. Notification of failure to comply will be accompanied by a report of errors associated with any submitted CRF. S3C Sequence Help Desk handles inquiries (contact info provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences and cure period for failure to comply with sequence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If any of the requirements are not satisfied at the time of filing or national stage entry, the applicant will be notified and given a period of time within which to comply in order to prevent abandonment of the application under 37 CFR 1.821(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to comply will result in abandonment under 1.821(g). Extensions of time may be obtained by filing a petition with the extension fee under 37 CFR 1.136. Applications will not be examined on the merits until a compliant Sequence Listing has been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect on international/PCT filings and actions by US ISA/IPEA
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Sequence Listing in ASCII plain text has not been submitted for an international application and the application is to be searched/examined by the US ISA/IPEA, a CRF must be submitted, accompanied by the late furnishing fee and a statement regarding identity or whether the CRF goes beyond the disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the required CRF is not timely provided, the US ISA shall search only to the extent a meaningful search can be performed without the CRF, and the US IPEA shall examine only to the extent a meaningful examination can be performed without the CRF.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRF may not be retained as part of the patent application file
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRF may not be retained as a part of the patent application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit CRF as required but expect it is not kept in the application file; follow USPTO submission/processing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of modified nucleotides (Appendix B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified bases may be represented as the corresponding unmodified bases in the sequence itself, if the modification is further described in numeric identifier <223> of the Feature section of the Sequence Listing. Symbols in Appendix B may be used in the description or Feature section but not in the sequence itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modifications not in Appendix B may also be represented as the corresponding unmodified base in the sequence itself, but the modification should be described using its full chemical name in the Feature section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide one-letter symbol requirement (Appendix A)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bases of a nucleotide sequence should be represented using the one-letter symbol for nucleotide sequence characters as provided in Appendix A (e.g., a, g, c, t, u, r, y, ... n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Appendix A symbol set for sequence entries; these are the standardized characters to represent nucleotides and ambiguity codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid three-letter symbol requirement and exclusion of D-amino acids (Appendix C/D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amino acids should be represented using the three-letter symbols with the first letter capitalized as provided in Appendix C. Those amino acid sequences containing D-amino acids are not intended to be embraced by this definition. Modified/unusual amino acids may be represented as the corresponding unmodified amino acids in the sequence itself if the modification is described in numeric identifier <223> of the Feature section (Appendix D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not show modified amino acids explicitly in the sequence; describe modifications in the Feature section. Use Appendix C three-letter codes for L-amino acids; consult Appendix D for modified amino acid symbols (which are not to be used in the sequence itself).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Feature keys for nucleotide sequences (Appendix E)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature keys related to nucleotide sequences (Appendix E) provide the allowed keys (allele, CDS, exon, intron, source, etc.) and descriptions for annotating sequence features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Feature keys as specified; the 'source' key is mandatory with at least a single source key spanning the entire sequence. Other keys describe regions, signals, binding sites, etc., and should be used where applicable in the Feature section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory Feature keys for protein sequences (Appendix F)
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature keys related to protein sequences (Appendix F) provide allowed keys (MOD_RES, MUTAGEN, TRANSMEM, SIGNAL, ACT_SITE, etc.) and descriptions for annotating protein sequence features and post-translational modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Appendix F keys to annotate post-translational modifications, active sites, domains, transmembrane regions, and other protein features in the Feature section; where descriptors are required, include them in the description field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WIPO ST.25 vocabulary for international compliance (numeric identifier <221>)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendices A–F reproduce Tables 1–6 of WIPO Standard ST.25 (2009). Applicants who file international applications or in countries that adhere to WIPO ST.25 should be aware that the data in numeric identifier <221> must use selections from Tables 5 and 6 of WIPO ST.25 to comply with that standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WIPO ST.25 terms are considered language-neutral vocabulary; if international compliance is desired, ensure <221> uses those selections even though 37 CFR requirements are less stringent.

rubrics_metrics.name: When multiple sequences/drawings exist, provide clear correlation between sequences and identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a sequence is presented in a drawing, reference must be made to the sequence by use of the sequence identifier either in the drawing or in the Brief Description of the Drawings, where the correlation between multiple sequences in the drawing and their sequence identifiers is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure drawings and Brief Description explicitly map each presented sequence to its SEQ ID NO to avoid examiner confusion and to comply with § 1.821(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and timing consequences tied to Sequence Listing compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications may be subject to reductions in patent term adjustment pursuant to 37 CFR 1.704(c)(13) if they are not in condition for examination within specified months; 'in condition for examination' includes compliance with §§ 1.821–1.825.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely and correct submission of Sequence Listings and CRFs affects examination timing and potential patent term adjustments; correct early compliance avoids abandonment and administrative penalties.
